lessons.title: Famous People
warmup: ⭐ Famous people
Name 3 famous people you admire. / 3 ta mashhur shaxs.
🏆 Achievements
What did they do that was special? / Ular nima qildi?

x: She is famous all over the world.
Winning gold is a great achievement.
He is a legend of football.

grammar.rule: Describe a person: **was born in / became / won / is famous for + -ing or noun**
grammar.uz: Shaxsni tasvirlash: 'was born, became, is famous for'
ex: He **was born in** 1954 and **became** a writer.
U 1954 yilda tug'ilgan va yozuvchi bo'lgan.
She **is famous for** winning gold medals.
U oltin medallar yutgani bilan mashhur.
I **admire her because** she helps children.
U bolalarga yordam bergani uchun qoyil qolaman.
mistake: Right: *She is famous for her work.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: He ___ born in 1980. (was/is)
She is ___ for her films. (famous/fame)
I ___ her hard work. (admire/admiring)
He ___ a gold medal. (won/wins)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: You admire someone. You say: → a) I admire her hard work b) She is boring c) Goodbye

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: in / born / He / 1954 / was / .
for / is / films / famous / She / her / .

reading.title: The Legend of Our School
reading.passage: Everyone at our school knows the name Bakhrom Xalilov. He was born in 1968 in a small village and walked four kilometres to school every day. He loved mathematics and worked hard. After school, he studied at university and became a famous engineer. He invented a cheap water pump for farmers — thousands of villages use it today. 'He is our school's legend,' our principal says. 'He shows us that a village boy can change the world.' I admire him because he never forgot where he came from.
qs: How far did Bakhrom walk to school?
What did he study?
What did he invent?
Why does the writer admire him?

listening.title: A Famous Athlete
qs: What sport does the athlete do?
When did she win her first medal?
What does she say about training?
listening.script: Listen. Our guest today is a famous swimmer. 'I was born in 2001 and started swimming at five. I won my first medal at twelve. My parents supported me always.' 'What is your secret?' 'Training every day, even when I don't want to. Dreams need work.'

writing.title: A Person I Admire
writing.task: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) about someone you admire: who, what they did, why you admire them.
writing.uz: Siz qoyil qoladigan shaxs haqida yozing.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your parents who they admire and why. Report. / Ota-onangizdan so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 famous-people words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about a famous person · Reading: re-read 'The Legend of Our School' · Speaking: describe your hero to your family.
teacher: Let students choose heroes they know — local pride.

lessons.title: Telling a Story
goals: 📖 Tell a story in the past
warmup: 📖 Story time
Tell a short story about yesterday. / Kecha haqida kichik hikoya.
🕰️ While...
'While I was eating, my phone rang.' What about you? / 'While' bilan gap tuzing.

x: While I was walking, it started to rain.
At that moment, the door opened.
When I arrived, they were leaving.
Men yetib kelganimda, ular ketishayotgan edi.

grammar.rule: **Past Continuous: was/were + -ing** for background action · interrupted by **Past Simple**
grammar.uz: 'was/were + -ing' — davom etgan harakat, o'tgan zamon — uni bo'lgan hodisa
ex: I **was reading** when the phone **rang**.
Kitob o'qiyotgan edim, qo'ng'iroq jiringladi.
While we **were walking**, it **started** to rain.
Yurib ketayotgan edik, yomg'ir boshlandi.
He **was sleeping** at that moment.
U o'sha paytda uxlayotgan edi.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: I was ___ (read) when it happened. (reading/read)
They were ___ (play) football. (playing/play)
She was ___ (sleep) at that moment. (sleeping/sleep)
While we ___ walking, it rained. (were/was)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: I ___ TV when the door opened. → a) was watching b) watch c) watched

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: reading / was / I / phone / when / rang / the / .
playing / were / They / football / .

reading.title: The Missing Key
reading.passage: Last Friday, I was studying in my room when I heard my mother calling: 'Have you seen my keys?' I was helping her look when my little brother walked in. While he was eating a biscuit, he suddenly stopped. 'What's in my pocket?' he asked. We looked — it was the key! He was playing with it in the morning and forgot. In the end, everyone laughed, and my mother put the key on a hook. 'From now on,' she said, 'keys stay on this hook!'
qs: What was the writer doing when mother called?
What was the little brother doing?
Where was the key?
What did mother do in the end?

listening.title: The Story of the Storm
qs: What was the family doing when the storm started?
What happened while they were watching?
What did they do in the end?
listening.script: Listen. Last week, while we were having dinner, a storm started. Suddenly, the lights went out. We were sitting in the dark when my father found candles. While he was lighting them, my little sister started to cry. 'Don't worry,' my mother said. 'This is an adventure!' In the end, we told stories by candlelight. It was actually fun!

writing.title: A Story from My Life
writing.task: Write a short story (6-8 sentences) using Past Continuous: what you were doing, what happened.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What were you doing at 8 last night?
What did you do in the end?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell a true story to your family using was/were + -ing. / Haqiqiy hikoya ayting.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 story words 3× · Grammar: 6 Past Continuous sentences · Reading: re-read 'The Missing Key' · Speaking: tell your story aloud.
teacher: Storytelling is the heart of B1 speaking.
This feeds L94 (storytelling circle) and L100.

We will do a short interview.

Plan the scenes: what the camera shows. / Sahnani rejalang.
Present your plan to the class. / Rejani taqdim eting.

practice.title: Build the Sentence

narrator / tells / the / story / The / .

speaking.body: Present your documentary plan: topic, 3 scenes, your role. (5-7 sentences) / Rejangizni taqdim eting.

lessons.title: Job Applications
warmup: 📝 Formal vs informal
How is a letter to a boss different from a letter to a friend? / Farqi?
💼 Your skills
What skills would you write in an application? / Qanday mahorat?

x: I want to apply for the job.
Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to apply...
My skills include computers and English.
I have two years of experience.

grammar.rule: Formal application: **Dear... → I am writing to apply for → my skills include → I am available → Yours sincerely**
ex: **I am writing to apply for** the position of assistant.
Yordamchi lavozimiga ariza yozyapman.
**My skills include** English, computers and teamwork.
Mahoratlarim: ingliz tili, kompyuter, jamoada ishlash.
**I am available** for an interview any day.
Suhbatga istalgan kun tayyorman.
mistake: Wrong: *I want the job. Give it to me.* (too rude)
Right: *I would be happy to work with you.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: Dear ___ , (Sir/Madam)
I am writing ___ apply for the job. (to/for)
My skills ___ English. (include/includes)
Yours ___ , (sincerely/sincere)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: A formal letter starts: → a) Dear Sir/Madam b) Hi c) What's up?

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: writing / apply / I / to / am / job / for / the / .
include / skills / My / English / .

reading.title: A Successful Application
reading.passage: When Zarina saw the job advertisement, she smiled. She had the right skills. She wrote a formal application: 'Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to apply for the position of shop assistant. I have one year of experience in a bookshop. My skills include customer service and computers. I am hard-working and responsible. I am available for an interview any day. Yours sincerely, Zarina.' The manager read it and thought: 'Clear, polite, confident.' He called her the next day.
qs: What job did Zarina apply for?
What experience does she have?
What does she say about availability?
What did the manager think of the letter?

listening.title: The Interview Call
qs: Why did the manager call?
What does he ask Zarina to bring?
When is the interview?
listening.script: Listen. Manager: 'Hello, is this Zarina?' Zarina: 'Yes, speaking.' Manager: 'This is Mr. Karimov. We liked your application. Can you come for an interview on Friday at 10?' Zarina: 'Yes, of course!' Manager: 'Please bring your qualification papers and a reference.' Zarina: 'I will. Thank you very much!'

writing.title: Write Your Application
writing.task: Write a short job application (6-8 lines): greeting, position, skills, availability, ending.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What job would you apply for?
A shop assistant or a waiter.
How would you end the letter?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Read one real job ad (online or newspaper) and list its requirements. / Haqiqiy e'lon o'qing.

quiz: How do you end a formal letter?
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 application words 3× · Grammar: write your own application · Reading: re-read 'A Successful Application' · Speaking: explain a job ad to your family.
teacher: Formal writing is a key B1 real-life skill.
Watch for informal tone in formal letters.

lessons.title: Email Writing
warmup: ✉️ Emails
How many emails do you write a week? / Haftada nechta email?
📧 Formal or informal?
An email to a friend vs to a teacher — different? / Farqi?

x: I sent the file as an attachment.
Save it as a draft first.

grammar.rule: Email structure: **greeting → purpose → details → closing** · formal vs informal tone
ex: Formal: **Dear Mr. Karimov, I am writing to inform you...**
Rasmiy: 'Hurmatli janob Karimov...'
Informal: **Hi Aziz! Just writing to say...**
Norasmiy: 'Salom Aziz!'
**Best regards / Yours sincerely**
'Hurmat bilan'
mistake: Wrong: email with no subject line

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: Write a clear ___ line. (subject/object)
I sent the file as an ___. (attachment/attach)
___ regards, Malika. (Best/Good)
I will ___ tomorrow. (reply/replay)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: A formal email starts: → a) Dear Mr. Karimov b) Yo c) What's up?

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: a / subject / write / clear / line / .
the / sent / I / as / file / attachment / an / .

reading.title: A Teacher's Email
reading.passage: Last week, our teacher sent an email to the class. The subject was 'Class trip — important!'. It said: 'Dear students, I am writing to inform you that the trip to Khiva is on Saturday. Please arrive at school at 7 a.m. Bring water and comfortable shoes. Reply to this email if you are coming. Best regards, Mr. Rahimov.' My friend replied: 'Hi Mr. Rahimov, I will come. Thanks!' We all smiled at his informal email — but the teacher didn't mind.
qs: What was the subject of the email?
What time must students arrive?
What should they bring?
What did the friend's reply say?

listening.title: The Email to the Manager
qs: Why is the girl writing?
What does she attach?
What does she ask?
listening.script: Listen. Girl: 'I need to email the manager. I'm writing to ask about the school project.' Friend: 'Attach your questions.' Girl: 'Good idea. Subject: Project questions. Dear Mrs. Azizova, I am writing to ask about the history project. When is the deadline? Please find my questions in the attachment. Thank you. Best regards, Nigora.' Friend: 'Perfect — clear and polite.'

writing.title: Write an Email
writing.task: Write an email (8-10 lines) to your teacher asking about homework or a trip. Use correct structure.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Who do you write emails to?
What's a good subject line for this?
Formal or informal to a teacher?

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Write one real email this week to a teacher or relative. / Bu hafta bitta email yozing.

quiz: Why is a subject line important?
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 email words 3× · Grammar: write a formal and an informal email · Reading: re-read 'A Teacher's Email' · Speaking: explain email structure to your family.
teacher: Real-life skill: students will write emails forever.
Show both formal and informal examples.
This builds on L95 formal writing.

lessons.title: Giving Advice
goals: 💡 Give advice with the Second Conditional
warmup: 💡 Advice time
A friend is sad. What do you say? / Nima deysiz?
🤔 If I were you...
'If I were you, I would rest.' What about you? / Siz nima qilardingiz?

x: If I were you, I would rest.
Can I give you some advice?

grammar.rule: **Second Conditional:** If I were you, **I would + verb** (imaginary advice)
grammar.uz: 'If I were you, I would + fe'l' — maslahat
ex: **If I were you, I would** rest more.
Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, ko'proq dam olardim.
**If I were you, I wouldn't** worry.
Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, xavotirlanmasdim.
Maybe **you should** talk to your teacher.
Balki o'qituvchingiz bilan gaplashishingiz kerak.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: If I ___ you, I would rest. (were/was)
If I were you, I ___ talk to her. (would/will)
I would ___ to the teacher. (talk/talking)
Maybe you ___ ask. (should/shouldn't)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: A friend can't sleep. You say: → a) If I were you, I would relax b) You are wrong c) Good night

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: you / If / were / rest / I / would / I / , / .
should / maybe / ask / you / .

reading.title: Ask the Teacher
reading.passage: A student wrote to the school advice corner: 'I am always tired. I can't finish my homework, and I am worried about my exams.' The teacher replied: 'Thank you for your letter. If I were you, I would make a plan. Do the most important homework first. I would also sleep eight hours — a tired brain can't learn. Maybe you should rest between lessons instead of looking at your phone. If you try this for two weeks, you will see a difference. Good luck!'
qs: What is the student's problem?
What should she do first, says the teacher?
Why is sleep important?
What should she do between lessons?

listening.title: Advice for a Friend
qs: What is the boy worried about?
What would the girl do if she were him?
What should he do before the test?
listening.script: Listen. Boy: 'I have a big test tomorrow and I'm worried.' Girl: 'If I were you, I wouldn't worry too much. You studied hard.' Boy: 'But I forget everything!' Girl: 'Maybe you should sleep well tonight. A rested brain remembers better.' Boy: 'You're right. I would sleep now.' Girl: 'Good idea. Good luck tomorrow!'

writing.title: Write Advice
writing.task: A friend is nervous about an exam. Write advice (5-7 sentences) using 'If I were you' and 'Maybe you should'.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: I can't find time to study.
If I were you, I would make a plan.
Maybe you should practice at home.
I would try again. You can do it!

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Give real advice to a family member using 'If I were you'. / Oilangizga maslahat bering.

quiz: Fill: 'If I ___ you, I would rest.' (were/was)
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 advice words 3× · Grammar: 6 'If I were you' sentences · Reading: re-read 'Ask the Teacher' · Speaking: role-play advice with your family.
teacher: Second conditional is a B1 milestone.
Drill 'If I were you, I would...' as a chunk.

lessons.title: Problems and Solutions
goals: 🗣️ Discuss what to do in difficult situations
Qiyin vaziyatda nima qilishni muhokama qilish
warmup: 🧩 Small problems
What little problems do you face at school? / Maktabda qanday kichik muammolar?
🔧 Solutions
What do you do when you lose your keys? / Kalit yo'qotsangiz?

x: How do you deal with stress?
We want to improve the situation.
If you try, you will succeed.

grammar.rule: Problems → solutions: **The problem is... / The best solution is to... / You should... / If I were you...**
ex: **The problem is** I have no time.
Muammo — vaqtim yo'q.
**The best solution is to** make a plan.
Eng yaxshi yechim — reja tuzish.
**If I were you, I would** ask for help.
Sizning o'rningizda bo'lsam, yordam so'rardim.
mistake: Wrong: *The solution is make a plan.*
Right: *The solution is to make a plan.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: The ___ is the noise. (problem/solution)
The best solution is ___ plan. (to make/making)
How do you ___ with stress? (deal/dealing)
You should ask for ___. (help/helping)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: A friend is tired all day. Best solution: → a) sleep more b) drink cola c) watch TV all night

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: problem / is / The / time / no / I / have / .
solution / is / to / plan / best / a / make / The / .

reading.title: The Crowded Bus Problem
reading.passage: Our bus is always crowded in the morning, and students are late. What is the solution? We discussed it in class. 'The problem is that there are too many students and too few buses,' said Akmal. 'The best solution is to add two more buses,' said Malika. 'Or we could start school ten minutes later,' suggested Timur. 'But that changes everything!' someone said. Our teacher smiled: 'Problems have many solutions. We need to choose the most practical one.' We wrote a letter to the bus company — and they answered!
qs: What is the problem?
What solution did Malika suggest?
What did Timur suggest?
What did the class do in the end?

listening.title: The Lost Phone
qs: What is the woman's problem?
What would the man do?
What should she do first?
listening.script: Listen. Woman: 'I can't find my phone!' Man: 'Where did you last see it?' Woman: 'In the kitchen, I think.' Man: 'If I were you, I would call it first. Then check the kitchen — maybe it's under a book.' Woman: 'Good idea. And if I don't find it?' Man: 'The best solution is to use a tracking app. You should set one up!'

writing.title: A Problem and Its Solution
writing.task: Write a paragraph (6-8 sentences): describe a problem you had and how you solved it.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What's your biggest problem at school?
Have you ever solved a big problem?
Yes, I found my lost dog!

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your family about a problem they solved. Report. / Oilangizdan so'rang.

quiz: Fill: 'The best solution is ___ a plan.' (to make/making)
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 problem/solution words 3× · Grammar: 6 problem-solution sentences · Reading: re-read 'The Crowded Bus Problem' · Speaking: discuss a problem with your family.
teacher: Practical life skills — students love solving real problems.
